summary: The opt-in Main ordinary-assignment path independently verifies authoritative obligations, snapshot and decision, then binds actual work/principal, requested configuration, input, generation, reservation and original fixed budget. Bounded evidence is staged in the existing content-addressed store before immutable route and intent; semantic-assignment and object-byte digests survive route/4, command/6, resolver readback, chunk transfer and runner launch equality. Historical plain preparation preserves its canonical bytes, while ordinary and causal wrappers retain validated route bytes. Terminal replacement recovery requires the exact persisted launch, a bounded canonical versioned session receipt with checksum and original inspector command identity, and a matching verified artifact. Duplicate launch and reconciliation recover the original terminal session without another provider invocation; terminal cancellation reports already terminal. Missing, corrupt or changed terminal proof retains reconciliation uncertainty, including historical records lacking the new receipt; spawn intent alone proves no terminal outcome. Unsupported launch tools/checks/resources and missing or changed assignment evidence refuse. Retained configuration and provenance remain supplied evidence rather than authenticated provider observations. Deferred output and independent review obligations hold native outcome acceptance. Focused fixtures cover byte compatibility, one invocation, terminal/session replay, corrupt or missing receipts, artifact-origin drift and missing terminal state. Actual real-PostgreSQL positive/crash/lifecycle execution, required exact-head CI and protected delivery remain separate evidence gates. This source does not establish installed matched Host/Runner adoption, preventive isolation, runtime containment, complete framework/Python-JavaScript journeys, parent acceptance or economic effectiveness. Terminal proof must be emitted from every actual terminal observation path, including reconciliation that completes before any observe call after lost launch output. Real PostgreSQL fixtures must record genuine ObservationRecorded results in the same order as ExecutionActor before resolving their next command: command identity includes journal revision, so omitting that event can reuse an already settled command and conceal actual recovery behavior. The source preserves both Observe-first and Reconcile-first terminal journeys with one provider invocation, original clocks and unchanged refusal controls. Exact replay uses the original persisted command bytes, identity and revision; semantic launch retry after journal advancement belongs to ExecutionSessionCoordinator and reconciles the existing attempt rather than requesting a new reservation-bound provider launch. Fixtures separately assert original-command duplicate persistence and wire replay, original session and reservation, and one invocation. A verified terminal cancellation emits the supported refused/no-effect disposition consumed as CancelRefused; missing proof or unobserved live termination remains unknown rather than being flattened into that refusal.
title: Ordinary assignment durable Main and runner source boundary
